newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dassault sees no curbs on Rafale weapons for UAE.
newsitem.headline: Dassault sees no curbs on Rafale weapons for UAE.

text.p: Dassault Aviation said on Friday it does not expect the French government to place restrictions on the weapons and electronic systems that can be supplied with the Rafale jet being offered to the United Arab Emirates (UAE).

The French interministerial group which authorises arms exports has not up to now prevented Dassault from selling the latest equipment for export, deputy chairman Bruno Revellin-Falcoz told reporters.
When asked if that would be the case for the UAE he said, "The same." The UAE wants the most advanced technology in its current competition for long-range combat aircraft.
The UAE has shortlisted the F16 Block 60 warplane from Lockheed Martin and the Rafale.
But U.S. political sensitivity over selling the most sophisticated arms and avionics systems could tip the balance in favour of the French firm, Gulf industry sources have said.
The competition is for up to 80 aircraft worth $6 billion.

Dassault has long boasted that France's value as an alternative arms source lies in its willingness to sell state-of-the-art weapons systems as the United States is selective over arms export approvals.
